lead: A skill tells the agent how to work. Open a card for when to use it and how it runs.

items.name: Work Desk
items.invoke: Paste a transcript, drop a file in inbox, or ask for the daily list.
items.summary: Turns messy talks into the morning board.
items.when: Transcripts, inbox files, Today, user groups, research, strategy, access, library, language, patterns, skills, branding, prototype, or Figma.
how: Read data/board.json first.
Fold the talk into that team's board.
Write board copy with Shaun writing.
Fold product words with UX writing.
Fold recipes with UX Patterns. Wait for Yes.
Fold studies with UX Research. Wait for Build plan.
Fold Figma library work with Figma. Live Astral first.
Check screen sizes with Responsive design. Wait for Yes.
Move processed inbox files to archive.
items.note: Do not invent groups, insights, or next steps a talk has not named. Never store a password.

items.name: UX writing
items.summary: Writes Astral UI copy with ORCA+ context.
items.when: Labels, buttons, errors, empty states, onboarding, tooltips, help, notifications, permissions, or modals.
how: Name the object, relationship, CTA, and attributes first.
Add role, intent, state, surface, locale, and risk.
en-GB-oxendict. Sentence case. Card subtext starts with a capital. Action-led CTAs.
The glossary outranks generic language guidance.
items.note: Do not invent product behaviour. Language entries stay the glossary.

items.name: UX Patterns
items.summary: Inspects the product, then recommends one change.
items.when: A flow, filter, create, select, overflow, scrollbar, library drift, or pattern check.
how: Inspect the product first.
Run the library check when the job is drift or a duplicate control.
Compare similar tasks.
Recommend one change.
Stop until you say Yes. Then prototype and record it.
items.note: Read-only until Yes. Product memory sits in docs/ux/. Native overflow lives in references/scrollbars.md.

items.name: UX Research
items.summary: Reviews what we already know before it plans a study.
items.when: What we know, what needs testing, build a study, analyse sessions, or update journeys and KEIs.
how: Search existing evidence first.
Name Known, Assumed, and Unknown.
Ask before creating a study.
Wait for Build plan before branded research files.
items.note: Never invent quotes, scores, or personas. Study memory sits in docs/research/.

items.name: Figma
items.summary: Keeps the IMSERV Design System file in step with live Astral.
items.when: Update Figma from the library or prototype, construct a component, or bind variables.
how: Inventory live Astral and the Figma file.
Map tokens and variants with the name table.
Construct one unmatched component from the construction notes.
Bind primitive and semantic variables.
Screenshot against live CSS. Check icon size, type size, font, placeholder copy, and placeholder icons. Ask them to Publish.
items.note: Coded library and prototype are the source of truth. Map, transform, then construct. Do not invent a CI or Storybook sync.

items.name: Responsive design
items.summary: Designs responsive behaviours, not smaller desktops. 1440 × 800 is the canvas. 1280 × 640 is the baseline.
items.when: Screen size, viewport, laptop, display scaling, zoom, reflow, breakpoints, panels or drawers, a squeezed graph, a crushed table, a clipped modal, a short window, or a small window.
how: Design against the browser viewport, not the monitor.
Write the responsive contract. Task, essentials, minimum working size, state to keep.
Read the screen. Find sidebars, fixed heights, transitions, and the scroll owner.
Check 1440 × 800, 1280 × 640, 1024 × 600, 1920 × 900, and 320 wide. Resize through each transition.
Report what holds, what breaks, and what state is lost at each size.
Recommend one fix. Shell and panels before shrinking. Wait for Yes. Then re-check all five.
items.note: Provisional target, not an industry minimum. No one has measured Astral users' viewports yet. A bigger monitor improves Astral. It is never required.

items.name: Shaun writing
items.invoke: Ask to write, rewrite, or review copy in Shaun's voice.
items.summary: Recognise, Shape, Reframe. Clear, human, useful.
items.when: Interface text, case studies, articles, or a tone check.
how: Recognise what the text is trying to do.
Shape it so the point is easy to hold.
Reframe so it sounds like a careful thought, not a generator.
items.note: Work Desk copy follows this skill. No colons, semicolons, or em dashes in board text.
